content: 1. Lamotrigine metabolism is increased when co-administered with certain drugs, potentially reducing lamotrigine levels by up to 50%. Adjust the lamotrigine dose as necessary when initiating, discontinuing, or modifying the dose of lopinavir/ritonavir. Monitor closely. 2. Lapatinib increases lopinavir levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 3. Lenacapavir increases lopinavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Lenacapavir may also increase the risk of adverse reactions to CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose. Monitor for potential toxicity. 4. Both lopinavir and lenvatinib prolong the QTc interval. Close ECG monitoring is recommended when co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 5. Letermovir increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 6. Lopinavir increases levamlodipine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely for symptoms of hypotension and edema. 7. Levoketoconazole increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid levoketoconazole doses exceeding 200 mg/day when used with lopinavir/ritonavir. 8. Lopinavir increases levomilnacipran levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 9. Lopinavir decreases linagliptin effects through mechanisms other than CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 10. Lopinavir decreases liraglutide effects, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor. 11. Both lopinavir and lofexidine prolong the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended. 12. Lorlatinib decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Lopinavir increases lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. No dose adjustment is required for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 14. Lopinavir increases lumateperone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 15. Lumefantrine may increase or decrease lopinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 16. Lopinavir increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust maraviroc dose to 150 mg BID to avoid toxicity. 17. Marijuana increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and lopinavir increases marijuana levels. Use caution and monitor. 18. Lopinavir increases mavorixafor levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Monitor QTc interval and adjust therapy as needed. 19. Lopinavir increases medroxyprogesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 20. Lopinavir increases meperidine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 21. Lopinavir decreases metformin effects, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor. 22. Methylprednisolone decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 23. Metronidazole increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 24. Miconazole vaginal increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Lopinavir and mifepristone both increase QTc interval. Obtain baseline ECG and monitor for QT prolongation and lopinavir-related adverse effects. 26. Lopinavir decreases miglitol effects, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor. 27. Mipomersen and lopinavir both increase hepatic enzyme levels, potentially leading to toxicity. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs). 28. Lopinavir increases mirtazapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 29. Lopinavir increases mirvetuximab soravtansine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor. 30. Mitotane decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for dosage adjustments when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. 31. Lopinavir increases mometasone inhaled levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. Use caution and monitor. 32. Lopinavir increases naloxegol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Monitor for adverse effects. 33. Lopinavir decreases nateglinide effects, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor. 34. Nefazodone increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and lopinavir increases nefazodone levels. Use caution and monitor. 35. Nelfinavir increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 36. Lopinavir increases netupitant/palonosetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 37. Nevirapine decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 38. Nifedipine increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and lopinavir increases nifedipine levels. Use caution and monitor. 39. Nilotinib increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 40. Lopinavir increases nimodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 41. Lopinavir increases nintedanib levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 42. Lopinavir increases nisoldipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 43. Lopinavir increases norethindrone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Lopinavir increases oliceridine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation. 45. Both lopinavir and olodaterol inhaled prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 46. Lopinavir and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid in patients with congenital long QT syndrome and monitor ECG closely. 47. Lopinavir increases osilodrostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 48. Both lopinavir and osimertinib prolong the QTc interval. Conduct periodic ECG and electrolyte monitoring. 49. Lopinavir increases ospemifene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and decreases ospemifene levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 50. Oxaliplatin increases lopinavir levels through mechanisms other than CYP3A4. Monitor ECG changes if therapy is initiated. 51. Oxcarbazepine decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 52. Both ozanimod and lopinavir prolong the QTc interval. Avoid initiating ozanimod in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs. 53. Lopinavir increases panobinostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce panobinostat starting dose to 10 mg if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 54. Lopinavir increases paricalcitol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 55. Both lopinavir and pasireotide prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 56. Pentobarbital decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 57. Phenobarbital decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 58. Phenytoin decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 59. Lopinavir increases polatuzumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 60. Posaconazole increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 61. Lopinavir decreases pramlintide effects, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor. 62. Lopinavir increases praziquantel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 63. Prednisone decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 64. Primidone decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
